football_evidence.question: Can UCF contain BYU’s explosive runs?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward BYU, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 5.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When UCF has the ball (big plays through the air): UCF’s offense turns 7.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and BYU’s defense gives up explosive gains on 5.5% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.3%).

When UCF has the ball (the line of scrimmage on running plays): UCF’s offense is stopped at or behind the line on 22.4% of its runs, and BYU’s defense stops 23.7% of opponent runs at or behind the line (FBS average 17.3%).

When BYU has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): BYU’s offense has allowed a sack on 1.9% of its dropbacks, and UCF’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
When UCF has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): UCF’s offense averages 6.8 yards per pass attempt, and BYU’s defense allows 5.6 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
contradicting: When UCF has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): UCF’s offense has allowed a sack on 4.5% of its dropbacks, and BYU’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.4% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.6%).
UCF comes in on 14 days of rest after an open week; BYU has had 6 days.
quarterbacks: Keyone Jenkins has completed 83 of 118 passes (70.3%) for 809 yards, 6.9 yards per attempt, 8 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for UCF, and has been sacked on 6 of 124 dropbacks.
Alonza Barnett III has completed 31 of 49 passes (63.3%) for 344 yards, 7.0 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception in two games for UCF, and has been sacked on 2 of 51 dropbacks.
Bear Bachmeier has completed 99 of 151 passes (65.6%) for 1,249 yards, 8.3 yards per attempt, 9 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in six games for BYU, and has been sacked on 3 of 154 dropbacks.
